prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one game ability VFX token atlas, 1024x1024 square RGBA with a truly transparent background. Exactly FOUR isolated hand-painted fantasy effect emblems in an exact evenly spaced 2 by 2 cell grid. Cell centers at 25% and 75% of image width/height. Keep each emblem entirely within the central 65% of its cell, with transparent gutters and no crossing between cells. No text, labels, frames, circles around icons, UI buttons, background, full characters, numbers, decorative borders, shadows or scenery. These are small rendered effect tokens and HUD icons; actual range shapes are rendered separately by the game. Strong distinct silhouette, detailed painted material, restrained glow, readable at 32px. Avoid large opaque panels. Depict characteristic tools/energy/material symbols, not a screenshot or miniature scene. Cell order: TOP LEFT passive, TOP RIGHT skill1, BOTTOM LEFT skill2, BOTTOM RIGHT ultimate. Original avatar: Koro Cloudtail. Character visual motifs: nimble simian scaffold builder with bamboo-jointed pole stilts, chalk measuring rope and light tool satchels; no monkey clone, spinning staff ultimate or extended auto-lock hits.
TOP LEFT: Measured Landing. Ability concept: landing on legal ground after his own vault grants Koro a 2 s balanced stance; next basic attack has a small shield break bonus. No stacking knockups.
TOP RIGHT: Plant Vault. Ability concept: plants a 2-HP pole at a legal ground point within 110 GU. It stands 5 s, visibly previews a 60-GU landing arc with a collision-tested endpoint. Max two poles.
BOTTOM LEFT: Pole Transfer. Ability concept: Koro or a **voluntarily consenting nearby ally** vaults from one pole to the previewed legal landing point after a 0.45 s windup. Cannot cross hard walls or tower-blocked zones, cannot initiate in hard CC, landing causes only a small radial shove (no full AoE knockup).
BOTTOM RIGHT: Scaffold Crossing. Ability concept: connects two poles with a visible elevated bamboo runway for 4 s. Eligible allies may **individually choose** to take one fast 65-GU arc between the poles. The crossing is not global teleportation; any pole destruction cancels later crossings, passengers already in flight resolve to nearest safe landing.
